gap: No result ChatGPT got puts strap length in one unit and one measure: Apple's Crossbody Strap runs 42.5–81.9 in (108–208 cm) of total length, while Bandolier's own adjustable straps run about 36–59 in (91–150 cm), so at full length Apple's is about 23 in (58 cm) longer. Bandolier counts 'strap length' as the whole strap, not the 'drop' where the case hangs.
standout_why: I compared against cameralookout.com (result 11 in the second chat), which already gives Apple's 42.5–81.9 in range and a CASETiFY Fidlock length of about 57.5 cm. It never converts them to one unit, never separates total length from drop, gives no Bandolier length, and says none of its products lists a load rating. I could not open the AppleInsider strap roundup (HTTP 403), so I can't rule out that it has some of this. The Bandolier product pages ChatGPT cited (Palmer Duet, Lily set) kept returning HTTP 429 and I could not read them. Bandolier's own blog does not give the Palmer chain's length.
decides: This is a partial finding. Tall shoppers, or anyone wearing the strap over a coat, get far more reach from Apple's strap: its longest setting goes past the longest Bandolier strap I could source (59 in). Apple's strap only fits select Apple cases and contains magnets. Peak Design's Micro Anchors fit any case with a strap loop, including most Apple iPhone 17 cases. That makes Peak Design the cross-brand pick if the shopper wants to keep a case they already have. None of the maker pages I opened publishes a load rating, so strap strength can't be compared.
